question.text:
Ice at $-20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is added to $50 \mathrm{~g}$ of water at $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, When the temperature of the mixture reaches $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C},$ it is found that 20 $\mathrm{g}$ of ice is still unmelted. The amount of ice added to the

water was close to (Specific heat of water $=4.2 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{g} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

Specific heat of Ice $=2.1 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{g} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$

Heat of fusion of water at $\left.0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=334 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{g}\right)$

solution.text:
Let m gram of ice is added. From principal of calorimeter heat gained (by ice) $=$ heat lost (by water)

$\begin{array}{l}

\therefore 20 \times 2.1 \times \mathrm{m}+(\mathrm{m}-20) \times 334 \\

=50 \times 4.2 \times 40 \\

376 \mathrm{~m}=8400+6680 \\

\mathrm{~m}=40.1

\end{array}$
